methodological_rigor.justification: Prospective multicenter single-arm phase 2 trial (SWOG S1512 cohort A, NCT02775851) with pre-specified primary endpoint (pCR rate), pre-planned central blinded pathology review by two pathologists, and pre-specified exploratory correlative WES analysis. The single-arm design is appropriate for this rare subtype but inherently limits causal inference; the authors explicitly acknowledge pCR-by-local-review as a limitation and addressed it through central review. Sample size was justified with a single-stage design powered at 90% to rule out a 5% null pCR against 25% alternative. Statistical methods are appropriate: one-sided Clopper-Pearson exact binomial for the primary endpoint, Kaplan-Meier with log-log CIs for survival, Nelson-Aalen for melanoma-specific survival with competing risks per Pintilie, reverse Kaplan-Meier for follow-up, and Wilcoxon for TMB comparison; CIs are reported throughout.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Findings are directly clinically relevant: a 71% pCR rate (95% CI 51-87%) with 87% 3-year OS and 95% 3-year melanoma-specific survival in a rare subtype where surgery is often morbid supports neoadjuvant single-agent pembrolizumab as a practice-informing option, with explicit implications for de-escalating surgery and avoiding adjuvant therapy. Two grade 3 AEs (7%) and no grade 4/5 events indicate an acceptable safety profile. As a non-randomized single-arm phase 2 cooperative-group trial, the Oxford CEBM LoE classifies as 2b (individual cohort study / low-quality RCT equivalent). The small sample (n=28) and lack of a comparator temper practice-changing strength, but findings inform guidelines and subsequent trials.

reporting_quality.justification: The manuscript reports a registered prospective clinical trial (NCT02775851), includes a CONSORT-style diagram (Fig. 1), describes enrollment dates, eligibility, protocol deviations, primary/secondary endpoints, adverse events per CTCAE v4.03, and references a Nature Portfolio Reporting Summary and full protocol in Supplementary Information. Key CONSORT items (trial design, participants, interventions, outcomes, sample size, statistical methods, flow, baseline data, outcomes/estimation, harms, limitations, registration, protocol, funding) are largely addressed. Data availability: source data are referenced for Figs. 3-6 and Extended Data Fig. 5, and WES correlative analysis is described with methods referenced to prior work, but no explicit repository accession is visible in the main text excerpt; protocol is provided in supplements. Minor gaps include explicit CONSORT checklist cross-referencing and granular repository identifiers in the visible text.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first prospective neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 trial specifically in desmoplastic melanoma, a rare subtype previously grouped with cutaneous melanoma in neoadjuvant studies. The 71% pCR rate materially exceeds historical pCR rates for single-agent neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 in cutaneous melanoma (19-25% per cited refs 6, 11, 12) and is comparable to combination regimens, filling a documented gap. Correlative WES confirming high TMB (median 62.8 Mut/Mb) and recurrent NF1/TP53/CDKN2A mutations extends prior retrospective observations (Eroglu 2018) into a prospective trial setting. Novelty is meaningful but constrained to a subtype-specific extension rather than a first-in-class mechanism, and the underlying hypothesis was drawn from prior retrospective data.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well organized into standard sections (Methods, Results, Discussion, Main) with clear, precise language and appropriate use of figures (CONSORT diagram, schema, waterfall, swimmer plot, KM curves, genomic oncoprint) and tables (baseline characteristics, AEs). Numerical results are consistently reported with 95% CIs and p-values, and discordant case narratives (e.g., PT0761, PT0785) add clinical nuance. The Discussion clearly contextualizes findings against SWOG S1801, NADINA, and prior neoadjuvant trials. Minor issues include some long, dense paragraphs and redundancy between Abstract, Results, and Discussion, but overall presentation is publication-ready.

key_strengths: Prospective multicenter cooperative-group phase 2 trial with pre-specified primary endpoint and appropriate single-stage design (90% power, null 5% vs alternative 25% pCR)
Primary endpoint met with 71% pCR (95% CI 51-87%, P<0.001) and excellent long-term outcomes (3-yr OS 87%, melanoma-specific survival 95%) with only 7% grade 3 AEs and no grade 4/5 events
Pre-planned central blinded pathology review by two pathologists with high concordance to local review (79% pCR+pPR centrally), strengthening primary endpoint credibility
First prospective neoadjuvant anti-PD-1 trial in desmoplastic melanoma, a rare subtype with distinct biology (high TMB, NF1 loss), addressing a documented gap
Correlative WES integrated with pathological response annotation, reinforcing mechanistic rationale (median TMB 62.8 Mut/Mb)
key_concerns: Single-arm design without randomized comparator limits causal inference relative to surgery-only or adjuvant-only standards
Small sample size (n=28 eligible) reduces precision, particularly for subgroup and genomic analyses (WES in only 16 patients)
pCR by local pathology as primary endpoint is acknowledged as a limitation; criteria for pathological response were developed ad hoc before INMC standards
Not all sites could provide surgical specimens for central review (3 missing), introducing potential selection in the central assessment
Data/code availability in the visible text is limited to figure source data; explicit repository accessions for WES data are not apparent in the main text excerpt
chief_reviewer.rationale: A prospective cooperative-group phase 2 trial in a rare melanoma subtype that met a pre-specified primary endpoint with a clinically meaningful 71% pCR rate, high long-term survival, and acceptable safety, supported by central pathology review and correlative genomics. These features plausibly support acceptance at the highest tier (Tier 1, e.g., Nature Medicine/Nature Cancer) with minor revisions to sharpen limitations and data-sharing statements.
